signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Bid
signals.text: AUD/CHF reflects a dominant G10 bilateral theme as AUD outperforms with a +1.294% weekly average while CHF lags at -0.764%. US military strikes in the Middle East and Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions have failed to ignite CHF safe-haven demand, with VIX at 14.4 signaling a low-volatility regime that favors carry. The AONIA-SARON carry differential provides a massive +442bp advantage for AUD/CHF, further supported by AUD COT LF net long positioning at the 95th percentile (z +1.92). AUD/USD remains technically robust, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7101/0.7016/0.6971), while USD/CHF tests resistance above its own SMA cluster at 0.8073/0.8087. Retail sentiment for AUD/CHF is at a 95% short extreme, providing a contrarian tailwind as the institutional long trend remains intact. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF; carry advantage and low VIX support trend continuation. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep for regional risk proxy. Risk: VIX spike above 25 triggers a sharp CHF safe-haven reversal.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Bessent Signal
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 160.12, breaching the critical 160.00 psychological level that has historically triggered BoJ/MoF action. Scott Bessent has recently described the yen slide as contained and expressed support for BoJ Governor Ueda, potentially signaling a coordinated policy stance ahead of the G20 summit. Despite the breach, the options market shows significant caution with a 1M 25d risk reversal at -1.74, signaling strong demand for JPY calls (USD/JPY downside protection). This options skew contradicts the flat spot momentum and the massive +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage. Technicals show USD/JPY holding above the SMA20 (158.87) but remaining below the SMA50 (160.84), suggesting a period of consolidation or policy-induced reversal. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; intervention risk at 160.00+ offsets carry advantage. Catalyst: G20 Finance Leaders' summit sidelines. Risk: BoJ holds and Fed's Warsh delivers a hawkish surprise, forcing a break toward 162.00.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT-OIS Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5920, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5910/0.5817/0.5850) ahead of this week's RBNZ decision. Speculative positioning is at a bearish extreme with COT LF net short -32,496, marking the 0 percentile of the 52-week range (z -2.60). This crowded short position directly contradicts the OIS market and bank research expectations for a 25bp hike on 2 September. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. The pair's resilience despite a 125bp Fed-RBNZ carry disadvantage suggests the market is already pricing the hawkish domestic data outlook. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; asymmetric squeeze setup against a 0-percentile spec short. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — 25bp hike expected. Risk: RBNZ holds rates steady, validating the crowded short and pressuring the 0.5850 support.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3540, effectively pinned to its SMA20 at 1.3540 and well above the SMA50/200 cluster near 1.3430. The options market is pricing significant tail risk, with 1M IV at 11.0% vs a 30-day realized volatility of only 4.9%. This creates a massive +6.1% Volatility Risk Premium (VRP), the highest among G10 majors, indicating that traders are paying a heavy premium for protection despite relatively stable spot price action. COT data shows GBP longs are crowded at the 96th percentile (lev_net +56,839, z +1.58), leaving the pair vulnerable to any dovish shift in BoE expectations or US data beats. The negative ESI for the UK (-9.2) further suggests the fundamental data is beginning to disappoint relative to high spec expectations. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish GBP/USD; high VRP and crowded longs suggest upside is expensive. Catalyst: US NFP on Friday. Risk: BoE shifts to a hawkish bias, justifying the crowded long positioning.
